chapters.title: Displaying the Professional Competence of a Human Figurine Vase
chapters.content:
"This maid is indeed a bit hot, and also a bit dizzy. Perhaps I'm on the verge of heatstroke."

Xiao Zheng was slightly surprised. Having expected to hear some cliché response, he hadn't anticipated hearing such a remark tinged with complaint.

Strictly speaking, he was entirely within his rights to charge Chunluo with the crime of showing disrespect to a superior, but the first thought that actually popped into his mind was that next time he painted, he should arrange an ice chest for her to beat the heat...

Xiao Zheng thought to himself that his temper seemed to have improved, or was it because he was somewhat drunk today?

With these thoughts, he unceremoniously reached out his free hand, touched Chunluo’s forehead, and nodded in confirmation: "It is indeed a bit feverish."

Then he ordered: "Su Youren, pour her a cup of herbal tea. Make sure she doesn't fall ill; I still want to paint her portrait in the next few days."

Having given the order, his hand didn't move away. Instead, it slid down, hooking Chunluo's chin to make her lift her face slightly.

"Looking at her from afar, she is bright like the rising morning sun; observing her up close, she glows like lotus flowers emerging from green ripples."

Xiao Zheng recited the compliment offhandedly, then let out a soft chuckle: "I really do want to see you..."

With her eyelashes lowered, Chunluo didn't quite catch the meaning: He wanted to see her? Or was there something else he left unsaid at the end?

Unfortunately, she couldn't figure it out and didn't dare ask, so she could only continue acting like a vase.

It wasn't until Su Youren personally brought over a cup of herbal tea that Chunluo was released. She was indeed genuinely thirsty; taking the tea, she drank two gulps in a row, and the bottom of the cup was already empty.

Just as she put down the teacup, she heard Xiao Zheng say: "Let's head back."

And so the entourage set off in the direction of the Hall of Mental Cultivation.

Compared to the leisurely journey on the way here, the trip back was far more lively.

Perhaps because the area hadn't been cleared out, the imperial procession successively encountered the Virtuous Consort (Xianfei), the Wise Consort (Defei), Noble Lady (Caren) Lu, Noble Lady Hu, Baolin Hua, Baolin Ying, Baolin Ning, Baolin Wan, Baolin Wang, and Baolin Mu. It was exceptionally bustling.

However, among these concubines, only the Virtuous Consort and the Wise Consort managed to cause the dragon carriage to pause for a moment. Even then, it was just a matter of a sentence or two, and none of them successfully invited the Emperor back to their own palaces.

By the time they returned to the Hall of Mental Cultivation, the sky was gradually darkening.

This time of day was when Chunluo and the other imperial palace maids had their evening meal. Xiao Zheng usually went to bathe at this hour, tended to by a different group of people.

Just as Chunluo was bowing out to leave, she happened to run into Su Youyi, the second-in-command among the eunuchs, who was passing by carrying a tray of green-backed identity tablets.

Currently, there were seventeen concubines in the palace in total, and having those green tablets neatly laid out still looked quite spectacular.

Chunluo curtsied slightly to let Su Youyi pass first.

Su Youyi paused, smiled, and said, "Is Chunluo-guniang heading to have her meal? I heard that one of the master chefs was itching to show off his skills today and whipped up a dish of pagoda pork. You'd better hurry over, or you won't even get to see that pagoda shape."

Chunluo smiled in response: "Many thanks for the reminder, Elder Brother Su-er. I should indeed hurry over and witness it."

After this brief exchange, the two of them passed each other, going their separate ways.

To be honest, back when Chunluo was still a mobile ornamental vase, Su Youyi hadn't been this polite. Encountering her, he would at most nod in acknowledgment and wouldn't bother trying to strike up a conversation to curry favor.

Now, however, because Chunluo showed faint signs of becoming a favored person in the imperial presence, people eager to cozy up to her naturally appeared.

Chunluo didn't find it disgusting; after all, it was human nature, and having more friends meant more paths. Who knew when she might find a use for him one day?

Pondering these things, Chunluo arrived at the dining area and found that her other colleagues had already arrived, though they hadn't started eating yet.

Seeing her, Xia Chan immediately called out, "Chunluo, you're here. Come quickly, look—pagoda pork."

Actually, the maids present weren't completely unfamiliar with it, but as palace maids, none of them had ever actually eaten pagoda pork before.

With Chunluo's arrival, everyone was present, so they readily took their bowls and chopsticks to divide up the pagoda pork.

Hmm... perhaps due to the reputation boost, it genuinely tasted a bit better than the other dishes.

After a hearty meal, everyone dispersed, each returning to their respective rooms.

After all, they had all been up since 3:00 AM and had bustled about all day; once dusk fell, it was time for sleep.

Walking alongside Xia Chan, Chunluo strolled slowly back to their quarters in the rear hall.

Before they could even cross the main hall, they saw Su Youren hurrying over: "Aish, Chunluo-guniang, His Majesty is summoning you. Quickly come with this servant."

Chunluo was baffled. It was already dark, and at this hour she would normally be off work! Why was she pulling overtime today?

Regrettably, she couldn't even mention overtime pay, so she could only obediently follow Su Youren into the main hall and further into the bedchamber.

The emperor's bedchamber was naturally huge, partitioned into two sections: the dragon bed and the couch.

Xiao Zheng was reclining sideways against soft pillows with a cold expression.

Some green-backed identity tablets were scattered on the floor, along with a teacup. Meanwhile, Su Youyi, whom she had just crossed paths with earlier, was kneeling on the ground, looking wretched and not daring to draw a full breath.

Chunluo felt a sudden thump in her chest. She could practically curse Su Youren to death in her heart: What kind of situation is this that you had to call me over?! Did you think kneeling a few extra people would look better?!

Unfortunately, she was already inside, and she could sense that Xiao Zheng’s gaze had landed on her.

Chunluo immediately bent her knees, lowered her gaze, and assumed the look she had been asked to make countless times during this period, fully manifesting the professional competence of a human figurine vase.

"This maid greets His Majesty."

Xiao Zheng gave an "en" sound, his tone tranquil: "Su Youyi, go to the Department of Reforming Criminals tomorrow to receive ten strokes of the paddle, and Su Youren, you go oversee the punishment. That's all, clean this place up, I'm going to bathe."

"Yes."

Chunluo instinctively prepared to withdraw along with the others, only to be called back: "Chunluo, come with me."

Stepping over the mess on the floor, Xiao Zheng walked outward with his hands behind his back.

Unable to help herself, Chunluo glared at Su Youyì—who was exhaling in relief after narrowly escaping disaster—before turning to follow.

Exhaling a breath, Su Youyi whispered, "Many thanks, Elder Brother Su, for saving my life."

Su Youren shook his head: "Don't thank the wrong person. If Chunluo hadn't happened to come over, I probably wouldn't be overseeing the punishment right now—I'd be right beside you getting beaten with the paddle."

Su Youyi sighed: "Both of you are my benefactors. Otherwise today... ugh, it was just a moment of stray thoughts on my part, thinking about the situation in the palace and boldly offering a couple of words of advice..."

Outwardly expressionless, Su Youren inwardly felt some annoyance at Su Youyi for running his mouth. His Majesty would favor whoever he wanted to favor; since they had already lost their male genitalia, as long as they served His Majesty well, what didn't they have? Why go sticking their noses into muddy waters?

Leaving aside the fact that those imperial consorts were not easy to deal with, His Majesty’s temperament simply could not tolerate any sand in his eyes!

Su Youren said sternly: "You'd better engrave this lesson in your memory. This time you acted out of public duty, so His Majesty merely punished you. If you really started flirting around with others, you'd be losing your life!"

Su Youyi naturally nodded repeatedly, hurriedly claiming he understood.

As the two of them chatted while cleaning up the mess in the room, Chunluo, who was trailing Xiao Zheng to the bathhouse, wasn't feeling nearly as relaxed.

Because the moment they stepped into the bathhouse, Xiao Zheng dismissed the attending palace maids with a wave of his hand, leaving only her behind.

Though the nannies had instructed Chunluo on what she was supposed to do during her etiquette training, she lacked practical experience!

After standing blankly for a moment and finally realizing she was supposed to undress Xiao Zheng, Chunluo discovered that he had already stripped off his clothes himself and stepped naked into the bath pool.

Mist curled in the air. Chunluo stood awkwardly to the side, pondering whether she should go over and scrub Xiao Zheng's back...

Instead, she saw Xiao Zheng raise a hand: "Get in, too."

He added: "Take off your clothes."

chapters.title: Xiao Zheng is not impotent, he just starts at zero frame?
chapters.content:
Chunluo stood frozen in place: What did "get in, too" and "take off your clothes" mean?! She clearly hadn't expressed any intention of climbing into his bed!

Seeing her motionless, a flash of irritation crossed Xiao Zheng's eyes: "Do I need to say it a second time?"

Chunluo gave a start, immediately stripped off her clothes, and stepped into the water.

Feeling somewhat nervous, she covered her front with one hand and her lower half with the other, slowly walking toward Xiao Zheng.

As she moved, the sound of splashing water—*swish, swish*—rang out.

Xiao Zheng’s face still bore no smile, and his gaze toward Chunluo remained entirely devoid of lust.

"I want to see what you look like when you're stirred with passion, but I don't want to give you a formal rank. Tell me, what should I do?"

Hearing this, Chunluo felt her anger flare right up to the top of her head. Wasn't this outright whoring for free?

The problem was, this scoundrel of an emperor had actually said it out loud! And he still wore the expression of someone negotiating a deal!

Yet, being a mere palace maid, could she possibly object?

Chunluo took a deep breath, forcing herself to calm down. Now...

The situation was simply too unfavorable. She had already come down completely naked, and if she failed to bed the emperor, she would likely be driven out of the Palace of Earthly Purity, or even lose her little life outright.

However, Xiao Zheng’s attitude was also very clear: he just wanted to get it for free. Even if she succeeded in bedding him, all her efforts would be in vain—she wouldn’t receive any imperial favor or title, and would remain nothing more than a movable vase in the Palace of Earthly Purity.

Damn it! (A plant)

This dog of an emperor clearly had something wrong with his brain!

Chunluo cursed and grumbled, wanting nothing more than to rush right up and punch his dog-like head in. But at the critical moment, reason prevailed after all—

Things had come to this, so she had to save her own skin first.

Chunluo forced out a smile: "This maid only wishes to serve Your Majesty. If I can serve Your Majesty in the Palace of Earthly Purity forever, it will be the greatest fortune of my life."

Xiao Zheng curled his lips at that: "Although these words sound a bit fake, they are pleasant to hear. Come closer."

Chunluo cautiously inched closer, and then the hand resting on her chest was suddenly pulled away. Xiao Zheng let out a "tch": "When I looked at you in the past, I figured they were big. Sure enough, they are big."

As he spoke, he reached out to caress her, and added a commentary: "Your skin is also very smooth. When I touched your face earlier, I was thinking that the phrase 'skin like congealed fat' might not even be enough to describe you."

Chunluo began to tremble slightly. Unlike her soul, which was a seasoned veteran, her body was completely inexperienced, and every move she made was naive.

It had even flushed an enticing pink.

However, Chunluo's mood was far from pleasant, because she clearly noticed: Xiao Zheng was merely looking at her, caressing her, and evaluating her, while his eyes held no trace of desire at all.

It was as if... he was carefully appraising and touching a pretty vase.

How could a person develop desire for a vase?

Chunluo’s brain was about to explode. What kind of bizarre specimen was this?! He made her take off her clothes and indicated he wanted a free ride, but could he please show even a tiny bit of infatuation or passion?

He was making it look as though she had zero attraction whatsoever!

Or perhaps...

Chunluo suddenly thought of a possibility: Could it be that Xiao Zheng was actually impotent and completely incapable of getting it up?!

Damn it! (A plant)

Why did the more she thought about it, the more she felt her guess was right?

Growing increasingly convinced, Chunluo could no longer maintain her coy and shy expression. She raised her eyes to glance at Xiao Zheng, her gaze filled with sympathy and ridicule—

Hahahaha, you're impotent! And you still want to get it for free? You can't even get it up, so why put on such a big front!

Xiao Zheng had been appraising her all along. Noticing her gaze, he also raised his eyes to look back.

Their gazes met in mid-air, and Chunluo instinctively lowered her eyelashes. There was no help for it; this was simply her instinctive reaction.

Through the hazy steam, Xiao Zheng didn't quite catch the look in Chunluo's eyes, but he suddenly grew interested. He moved the hand that had been lingering on her waist and cupped Chunluo's face to examine it closely.

Actually, he had already examined her several times, but every time he looked, he found something new.

For instance, this time, her eyelashes—dampened by the mist—were clearly defined, dark, and curled upward. Her lips were the same, becoming even more rosy and tender under the mist, looking somewhat like a pink cherry that wasn't quite ripe.

Xiao Zheng leaned forward and bit down on it, not using any force, just lightly nibbling.

Naturally, there was no sourness or sweetness of a cherry, but it felt like biting into a cloud—extremely soft.

Xiao Zheng leaned forward once more, coming into intimate contact with this soft cloud, and gradually escalated it into a breathless, intense kiss.

Dizzied by the kissing, Chunluo in a daze seemed to brush against something and gave a start from the heat. Then she suddenly realized that was Xiao Zheng's "weapon," and she felt somewhat...

Ah, so she guessed wrong at the very beginning?

He was looking at her body without any desire at all just a moment ago, so how did he manage to get it up in the time it took for a single kiss?

Wasn't Xiao Zheng impotent? Was he just capable of zero-frame startup?

Chunluo's head was buzzing, partly from a slight lack of oxygen due to the kissing, and partly because... Xiao Zheng was kissing her collarbone, his hands not idling as they roamed everywhere.

Compared to the previous caresses, this time carried a different kind of meaning, and Chunluo's inexperienced body couldn't handle it at all. She shivered and shrank instinctively, yet she also had to follow the instructions of her soul and wanted to open herself up.

Xiao Zheng seemed very satisfied with her reaction. He let out a low chuckle, then scooped Chunluo up in his arms and carried her out of the bath.

Chunluo, who had already steeled herself, was slightly annoyed: ...What is it now? A mandarin duck bath wasn't enough to satisfy you?!

Besides, being carried around stark naked and walking through this spacious hall was extremely humiliating, you know!

Unfortunately, Chunluo had no control over Xiao Zheng's actions whatsoever.

Soon, Xiao Zheng stopped. He placed the person in his arms onto a small couch and reached out to grab a nearby towel to dry his body.

Chunluo lowered her eyes, putting on an expression of being too shy to look at his naked body. But inwardly, she was practically speechless to the extreme—which weirdo does it with someone and suddenly stops halfway through to dry off water droplets?!

Yet as he dried himself, Xiao Zheng kept talking: "I just remembered you're a virgin. It wouldn't do to stain the bathwater with blood, so we should go to the bedchamber instead. You should dry off too; you're dripping wet."

Finding it hard to pretend she didn't hear, Chunluo had no choice but to curl her body up very awkwardly, covering her chest with one hand while reaching for a towel with the other.

Xiao Zheng suddenly chuckled and said, "You look a bit foolish like that."

The soul of Chunluo—who had never stepped into a public bathhouse and whose intimate interactions with others had strictly been limited to turning off the lights—thought: ...Fine, fine, it's just us time-travelers who aren't as thick-skinned as you!

Internally complaining, Chunluo dried herself off in a flurry, then wanted to pick up the clothes on the floor to put them back on—it wasn't that she didn't care about hygiene, but mainly because she couldn't possibly walk around naked to find clothes in her own room, right?

Xiao Zheng grabbed her abruptly, pulling her straight into his arms. His hands began to wander restlessly again, while he calmly said: "If you dare to put on those dirty clothes, I'll have you transferred to the Laundry Bureau by tonight."

Chunluo: What's dirty about them? They were clearly the new ones she had changed into today, and they had only been on the floor for a brief moment. The hall was cleaned twice a day, and it was clean enough that there wasn't even a speck of dust, alright?

With no human rights, however, she didn't dare to refute or argue back at all.

Chunluo took a deep breath and asked in her usual soft, delicate voice, "Then what should this maid wear?"

Xiao Zheng didn't answer. Instead, he took matters into his own hands—

He wrapped her voluptuous figure in a bath towel, scooped her up in his arms once more, walked out of the bath, and headed straight for the bedchamber—the best viewing posture for the vase.

chapters.content:
luo buried her face in his chest, having zero desire to see which colleagues she might run into along the way.

At the same time, she was somewhat surprised. Xiao Zheng's physical stamina seemed quite good; she weighed a little over a hundred pounds after all. Although she wasn't quite a hundred and twenty, she certainly wasn't light by any measure.

Yet carrying her seemed effortless for Xiao Zheng, and his strides were long and steady, without the slightest strain.

And thinking back carefully, this man also had pectoral muscles, abdominal muscles...

Tsk, you couldn't tell at all under normal circumstances!

Chunluo thought with sorrow: If she was already destined to be had for free, she could only take comfort in the fact that Xiao Zheng had the strength, the skill, and the handsome face.

Moreover, as the night breeze blew, Chunluo's mind cleared up a bit. Although Xiao Zheng said he wouldn't give her a title or rank, what if she got pregnant?

The situation in the palace wasn't good, and pregnancy wasn't the best choice, but if she did get pregnant, they would surely have to grant her a rank that required her to wake up at 5:00 AM, right?

Chunluo sighed inwardly. Xiao Zheng's free-ride operation genuinely made her feel that waking up at 3:00 AM was almost acceptable.

She had no idea what was going on in this man's head. She had honestly and obediently played the part of a movable decorative vase, never even casting a flirtatious glance at him. Normally, she was even extra cautious and never cracked any witty jokes.

After much deliberation, Chunluo figured it was probably the fault of the [Skin Like Congealed Fat] and [Eyebrows Like Painted Mountains] traits.

Although she wasn't the absolute prettiest among the emperor's harem concubines, these two traits might have just struck Xiao Zheng's fancy?

Sigh, she regretted it just a tiny bit...

Chunluo quietly asked the system: [Hey System, is there any regret pill in the mall? Or items like time reversal?]

System: [No.]

Chunluo sighed heavily: [Sigh, you intergalactic mega-corporations are useless too. You can already travel through time and space, so why didn't you invent a time-reversal gadget?]

System: [...This isn't a matter of whether it's possible or not, but rather that the laws of the universe do not allow it.]

Chunluo still wanted to chat for a bit, but they had arrived at the bedchamber.

Xiao Zheng placed her on the dragon bed and began to strip off his clothes.

Chunluo watched with her own eyes as he transformed from a well-dressed man into a handsome, naked one—and his "weapon" was already fully erect!

For some reason, her mental state slightly collapsed, and driven by some inexplicable impulse, she rolled across the bed... which happened to make her miss Xiao Zheng's reaching hand...

Uh (⊙o⊙)... Chunluo hadn't expected the timing to be this precise.

Lying on the bed, she glanced at Xiao Zheng, whose expression held a trace of bewilderment, and for some inexplicable reason, she really wanted to laugh—

No, hold it in. Laughing out loud right now might cost her her life.

Yet Xiao Zheng's habitually cold and aloof face suddenly displaying a dazed expression was genuinely hilarious!

(*＾-＾*)

"Hahaha..."

Chunluo still failed to hold it back, letting out three laughs before quickly covering her mouth and rolling over to turn her back to Xiao Zheng, her shoulders shaking uncontrollably.

The muffled chuckles were painfully obvious in the quiet bedchamber.

Xiao Zheng had already reassembled his expression, maintaining his usual cold aloofness, though a spark of fire lingered deep within his eyes.

It wasn't a fire of burning rage, but rather a fire born of overwhelming desire.

The moment Chunluo laughed just now, only two phrases had crossed his mind: bright eyes and white teeth, a captivating and radiant smile.

The face that usually looked as calm and light as a landscape painting had suddenly sprung to life, both exquisite and charming.

Compared to those minor flaws, Xiao Zheng chose to completely ignore them.

Meanwhile, lying on her side, having finally swallowed her laughter and left with only terror, Chunluo had no idea that the 50 points she had spent earlier had just saved her life.

Just as she was about to drop to her knees and beg for mercy to salvage her little life, the towel wrapped around her was pulled away. Then, a muscular torso with well-defined planes pressed against her back, and a familiar, large hand once more caressed her waist...

╭(′▽`)╯╰(′▽`)╮

At 3:00 AM, her powerful biological clock woke Chunluo up.

She didn't move, nor did she even open her eyes. Everything that had happened last night remained vivid in her mind; she was currently sleeping in the coveted dragon bed.

Even though ever since Xiao Zheng announced he wanted a free ride, she hadn't wanted to climb the dragon bed at all, facts surpassed thoughts—she had successfully climbed it.

Sigh, and there was nothing special to say even after succeeding; she was still just a palace maid with zero human rights.

The mere thought of this status—one she had struggled for so long to shake off—made Chunluo want to sigh again, but she held it back, because people who sighed too often brought bad luck.

Better think on the bright side—

After all, she got to sleep with a man who had such a great physique, such good skills, and such a handsome face. When things ended last night, he even personally wiped her body and changed her into sleeping garments. What a pity he was a communal property shared by a bunch of people... Sigh!

Let's think on the bright side again—

Although she hadn't bought fertility pills from the system mall last night, both of them were young and robust, so maybe she got pregnant? But then again, she'd probably be forced to drink a bowl of contraception soup the moment she got up... Sigh!

Chunluo found that she simply couldn't stop sighing!

After her wild train of thought, drowsiness overtook her once more, so she simply emptied her mind and plunged straight back into a deep sleep.

As a result, when Chunluo woke up again, she found Xiao Zheng being dressed and washed by a group of attendants.

How should she put it? At that moment, a chill of escaping souls went straight up to her crown.

Chunluo practically rolled off the dragon bed. The moment she hit the floor, she dutifully dropped to her knees with a heavy, dull thud.

Hearing the sound, Xiao Zheng looked over, his tone cold: "At least you didn't sleep until the sun was high in the sky."

Lowering her eyes and concealing her gaze, Chunluo instinctively assumed the vase's optimal viewing posture, her voice as thin as a mosquito's: "Please forgive me, Your Majesty. This maid knows her wrong."

Xiao Zheng ignored her, letting the attendants adorn him with accessories and comb his hair, while also letting Chunluo stay on her knees, unmoving and truly looking like a vase.

After about a quarter of an hour of grooming, Xiao Zheng finally said leisurely: "Alright, get up."

Chunluo scrambled briskly to her feet, only to hear Xiao Zheng give an order: "Su Youren, tidy up the left side chamber for her to live in, and go to the storehouse to pick out a pair of mutton-fat jade bracelets. Everything else remains as usual."

Chunluo understood. Having worked hard for a whole night (?), she had earned a single room and a pair of jade bracelets, yet she remained an imperial attendant maid.

Fine, whatever. Things couldn't get any worse anyway.

As for the group of attendants around who heard the order, they all wore looks of astonishment—after all, quite a few palace maids in the Palace of Earthly Purity had attempted to climb the dragon bed and put it into action, but those people were generally chased off to the Laundry Bureau to wash clothes.

Oh, there was one who succeeded, but she was sent to the Shuiyun Taoist Temple to become a nun!

Yet Chunluo was different. Although she wasn't granted a formal title, she wasn't driven away either. And did the emperor's words mean she didn't have to drink the contraception soup? In that case, wasn't there a chance she might conceive an imperial heir?

Moreover, Chunluo had been arranged to live in the left side chamber of the Palace of Earthly Purity—wasn't that taking the lunar prize first just by being close to the water?

One could easily imagine what kind of sensation this news would cause once it spread!

Chunluo herself realized this point, and immediately began worrying about her own little life once more.

Then, Xiao Zheng spoke again: "Su Youren, seal off the news. Inform the Bureau of Imperial Bedchambers to record the tally in the secondary register; there's no need to submit it to the Empress at the end of the month."

"Understood."

Su Youren acknowledged the order with a stiff scalp, feeling the task was immensely arduous. After all, the emperor had favored a maid from the Palace of Earthly Purity, and there was simply no way to keep this news hidden from the servants within the palace.

Even if he forcefully suppressed the news, it probably wouldn't stay hidden for long.

Right now, he could only pray that Chunluo would quickly manage to coax the emperor into granting her a formal rank so she could move out, or perhaps that the emperor would grow tired of her and kick her out of the Palace of Earthly Purity.

Had Chunluo—who was burdened with high hopes and simultaneously cursed by this silent judgment—known any of this, she would have given him five words: Heh, keep dreaming.

chapters.title: For now, better hook Xiao Zheng's gaze first
chapters.content:
The emperors of the Qianyuan Dynasty typically woke up at five in the morning, heading to the imperial study at six to summon key ministers to formulate strategies for the major issues to be addressed during the morning court session, before attending court at seven.

When there were many affairs, court would dismiss at nine; when there were fewer affairs, it would dismiss whenever appropriate.

Xiao Zheng appeared to be a self-disciplined and diligent emperor. At least ever since Chunluo arrived at the Palace of Earthly Purity, he hadn't missed a single morning court session. Forget single or double days off—he hadn't even taken a break on the Holy Mother Dowager's birthday.

Consequently, at six in the morning, Xiao Zheng headed to the imperial study as usual.

Chunluo finally earned a moment to breathe.

Su Youren commanded a crowd of people to scurry about: they needed to warn everyone in the Palace of Earthly Purity not to run their mouths, search the storehouse for items, and clean up the left side chamber. All three tasks had to be completed before the morning court session ended.

None of this had anything to do with Chunluo. Although she nominally remained a palace maid, she had never done any chores before, and she certainly wasn't going to start doing them now.

Chunluo wandered around the courtyard of the Palace of Earthly Purity for a few turns before returning to her room to pack her belongings.

Xiacia was the maid specifically responsible for brewing tea, and she was also free at this hour. However, unlike before, her attitude reverted to the cold indifference she had shown at the very beginning.

Chunluo had expected this.

After all, Xiacia’s attitude toward her had only turned warm because she hadn't wanted to climb the bed...

Now that she had been slept by Xiao Zheng, they were no longer walking the same path, sigh.

Chunluo sighed as she packed, wondering when her single room would be ready... Wait, once she moved out, wouldn't Xiacia get to enjoy a single room all to herself?

What was going on? She was the one who suffered hardship, yet her unfamiliar roommate Xiacia got to enjoy the benefits?!

Come to think of it, Xiacia had been living in a single room even before she arrived, right...

Chunluo had never realized she could be so slow-witted. Had her brain completely stopped functioning before? Such an obvious fact, and she was only just noticing it now!

Thinking deeper, none of the other imperial attendants had single rooms, but Xiacia did.

And as for her, she had gotten her single room by trading her chastity!

Then, what had Xiacia traded? Surely it wasn't also...

Chunluo suddenly felt her scalp tingle. This dog of an emperor truly specialized in eating the grass near his own nest!

As the saying goes, when you spot one cockroach... therefore, perhaps the other imperial attendants had also been slept by him, only for Xiao Zheng to lose interest in them afterward, prompting him to revert them to sharing double rooms.

This truth was somewhat thrilling. Chunluo sat down flat on the bed, staring blankly in a daze: She had a feeling she would eventually end up just like them...

Forget about failing to get a promotion, a raise, or escaping the torture of waking up at 3:00 AM as a palace maid; why did she also have to go through a round of being played with and then discarded?

There was no living like this!

Driven by frustration, malice welled up in Chunluo's heart. Since the dog of an emperor couldn't keep his lower half under control, she might as well disable him right here and now!

[System, are there any items that can cause a man to lose his sexual function?]

The system's data-chin nearly dropped to the floor. It asked: [...Host, could you first explain who you plan to use it on?]

Chunluo gave a light snort: [There's only one man in this palace besides the eunuchs, who else do you think?]

Regaining its composure, the system replied in a rigid voice: [As the emperor of this world, Xiao Zheng is the core of its stable development. Enchantment items, offensive items, and any items that pose a potential hazard to his life cannot be used on him.

Well, cause-and-effect items are fine—such as the [Lucky Halo]—but such items inherently pose no threat.

Furthermore, as a time traveler, if you directly or indirectly cause widespread devastation in this world, it will likely trigger the system's built-in arrest protocol. Your soul will then be extracted, you'll be dragged back, and you'll probably end up thrown into the eighteenth level of hell or something similar.

Host, although the laws and regulations in your current environment are somewhat lacking, we still hope you can strive to be a kind person.

This system rather enjoys skimming and slacking off during business trips and doesn't want to go back to a 996 schedule too early. Thank you.]

Chunluo fell silent: ...There were too many complaints to voice, yet chewing on it, it actually made a bit of sense.

So she concluded: Life really couldn't go on like this!

Just as Chunluo was feeling depressed, suffocated, and on the verge of an outburst, Xiacia spoke up—

Her tone was detached: "Chunluo."

Chunluo turned her head to look at her.

Xiacia continued: "Are you feeling very pleased right now? What a pity. In the Palace of Earthly Purity, once you are favored, you either move out to become a mistress, or you get driven out to become a nun at Shuiyun Temple..."

Chunluo pressed her lips together, thinking that her previous guess seemed to have been wrong again. Perhaps that unreliable brain of hers really wasn't worth keeping.

Xiacia sighed: "My elder sister was..."

If you are favored, you won't be sent to the Laundry Bureau; going to the Shuiyun Taoist Temple is just a bit more secluded. But if you become a master yourself, you had better look after your own future."

Chunluo understood. Among those in the Hall of Mental Cultivation who tried to climb into the emperor's bed, if Xiao Zheng didn't sleep with them, they would be sent to the Laundry Bureau to wash clothes. Don't think this job was simple; all the clothes in the entire palace were washed by them, and they used cold water year-round. It was even more tormenting than sweeping floors.

But if Xiao Zheng accepted them with a smile, there would be two outcomes—either become a imperial concubine or become a nun.

...Hearing this made Chunluo regret it to her very core.

Had she known, she would have stayed in the Baohua Hall. Although the Baohua Hall was dilapidated and had a bleak future, at least she wouldn't be caught in this dilemma of being unable to advance or retreat like now.

Chunluo felt even more depressed.

Around eight o'clock, Su Youren personally came over and politely escorted Chunluo to the left side room.

He also presented a pair of mutton-fat white jade bracelets.

Chunluo accepted them with a lack of enthusiasm, gave a perfunctory expression of gratitude, closed the door, and collapsed onto the newly made bed, feeling utterly lifeless.

That is to say, how on earth was she supposed to turn her situation around now?

Chunluo really didn't want to be a palace maid for the rest of her life, and especially didn't want to become a vegetarian nun by taking vows. Shouldn't she take precautions against a rainy day right away?

Otherwise, should she buy fertility pills and test whether getting pregnant would allow her to make a comeback and sing a triumphant song?

After all, having a child would surely grant her some dignity, right?

If she gave birth to an imperial prince, she could kick Xiao Zheng aside, focus on turning the prince into the emperor, and then make a leap to become the Holy Mother Dowager Empress, still enjoying a life of ease.

It just took a bit too long and carried rather high risks.

Chunluo frowned. She wasn't the kind of person who pinned all her hopes on someone else. The mere thought of having to rely on a son to rise in power, or relying on Xiao Zheng's charity for a shred of dignity, made her feel deeply uncomfortable.

Well, to put it accurately, she simply refused to submit.

After grumbling to herself for a while, Chunluo decided she would wait and see how things developed first.

They say that when matters are delayed, they tend to smooth out, and besides, she truly had no other tricks up her sleeve.

Sigh.

Sighing, Chunluo got up from the rumumbled bed, tidied up casually, and sat before the dressing table to paint her eyebrows.

For now, the best strategy was still to hook Xiao Zheng's attention first.

At least she couldn't become a nun—braised pork was her—[

chapters.title: People who do good deeds die early to be reincarnated, people who do evil deeds go down to the eight
chapters.content:
Chunluo drew the misty eyebrows of Sister Daiyu.

This signaled that she had sacrificed her chastity without receiving a corresponding reward (such as an official rank), and thus harbored a faint sorrow in her heart.

Having finished her eyebrows, Chunluo picked up the mutton-fat jade bracelets to examine them. She didn't understand jade, but they looked lustrous and felt smooth to the touch. Since her wrists were completely bare, she might as well put them on.

One on each wrist, she instantly felt her wrists grow much heavier.

After that, Chunluo walked out and dutifully stood in the courtyard corridor, waiting for Xiao Zheng to return from morning court.

She even adjusted her positioning to ensure that the moment Xiao Zheng glanced over from the entrance, he would immediately see her picture-perfect beauty. Heh, a human-shaped vase had to be this dedicated.

Just as Chunluo settled into her spot, three rhythmic whips cracked outside.

Shortly after, Xiao Zheng, clad in a dragon robe, walked in with his hands clasped behind his back, looking rather displeased.

Chunluo didn't look closely, immediately bending her knees in a curtsy. The other palace attendants in the courtyard did the same, executing the gesture with absolute uniformity.

Xiao Zheng did not tell them to rise. He strode over to the corridor in a few steps, reached out to pull Chunluo up, and walked straight into the inner room.

Not until the sound of footsteps completely vanished did the bowing attendants stand up, exchange glances, and then go back to what they were doing.

Chunluo followed closely behind as her wrist was pulled, but she very cautiously lagged one step behind Xiao Zheng.

Once inside the room, Xiao Zheng sat down on the daybed, pulling Chunluo down to sit right beside her.

Extending his hand, Xiao Zheng slid his fingers from Chunluo's wrist up to her arm, even giving it a pinch.

Chunluo felt a secret resentment: Who designed these palace maid uniforms? Why were the sleeves designed so loose? It gave him the chance to take advantage of her! And for free, too!

Yet she couldn't even fight back. Sigh!

"Sigh..."

Chunluo startled, thinking she had let out a sigh of her own, before realizing it was Xiao Zheng who had sighed.

She was utterly speechless—she was the one with a bleak future and she hadn't even sighed yet!

Having finished her mental complaint, Chunluo decided to be a bit bolder: "Your Majesty, why are you sighing?"

*(≧▽≦*) Hehe, spit it out so it can make me happy too!

Xiao Zheng glanced at her, leaned back lazily, and said in a calm tone, "I am considering whom to choose."

As he spoke, he continued to toy with Chunluo's hand.

Chunluo purposely furrowed her brows and pressed on: "Choose whom? Is there something that needs to be done?"

Since Xiao Zheng had been watching her all along, he instantly noticed her unfamiliar eyebrow shape. While carefully examining them, he spoke indifferently, "I am twenty-five years old, yet I have no sons to my name. Both the imperial court and the inner palace are pressing me—what do you think needs to be done?"

Chunluo's heart fluttered with unease; she had a lingering feeling this topic was not suited for further discussion.

Before she could open her mouth to ask more, however, Xiao Zheng changed the subject: "Your eyebrows look fresh today, like a beauty from Jiangnan, though your clothes don't quite match."

Chunluo thought the next step would be him rewarding her with pretty fabric to make new clothes, but instead...

Xiao Zheng said, "It is a pity you cannot wear other garments, so I can only strive to ignore what you are wearing."

Chunluo: ...If she were to vomit blood and die, there was no need to doubt it—she would have been angered to death by this bastard emperor.

Perhaps because she was too angry, a trace of it leaked onto Chunluo's face.

"When you are angry, the outer corners of your eyes droop. It actually doesn't look bad."

Such was Xiao Zheng's commentary.

The party being reviewed, Chunluo: ...Damn it!

"Your Majesty, do you always talk like this on ordinary days?"

Had this wretched mouth of hers truly never been beaten up? Oh right, indeed no one dared to beat an emperor.

Xiao Zheng curled his lips into a smile, his voice turning cold: "You've grown quite bold, even daring to speak in sarcasm."

"This maid wouldn't dare, this maid was merely curious."

Chunluo was not frightened in the least, seeing as Xiao Zheng was smiling; it was obvious he was deliberately trying to scare her with a cold tone.

"Usually, those who dare to talk back to me are people I never see again. Care to guess where they went?"

Having said that, Xiao Zheng waited at his ease for Chunluo's reaction.

Chunluo replied with a hesitant tone: "People who do good deeds die early to be reincarnated, and people who do evil deeds go down to the eighteenth layer of hell?"

"Hahaha... Your answer is quite amusing!"

Chunluo also offered a faint smile. Of course, after all, she already knew that dealing a malicious blow to him meant a direct ticket to the eighteenth layer of hell.

"This maid is only speaking the truth. Surely Your Majesty wouldn't feed and house someone who talks back with good food and drink?"

Xiao Zheng's smile did not fade as he said, "As it happens, there really are such people. Doesn't the Censorate raise several dozen of them?"

"Your Majesty is truly magnanimous and benevolent."

"..."

Xiao Zheng reached out and pinched the flesh of Chunluo's cheek, his tone unkind: "Speak properly. Did I ask you to flatter me?"

Chunluo deliberately puffed out her cheeks, pushing against his large hand while saying, "Your Majesty sees clearly; this maid is entirely sincere. Had Your Majesty not been magnanimous, this maid would probably be drinking Meng Po's soup and heading off to reincarnation by now."

Xiao Zheng could not help but smile: "I've only just discovered that when your tongue is sharp, you speak even better than those flattering ministers. Before, you looked so taciturn and overly cautious—you were really putting on an act!"

Chunluo blinked her innocent almond-shaped eyes: "This maid is clearly loyal and devoted, so how could I compare to flattering ministers? Besides, before... this maid was merely guarding her proper place."

"Then why aren't you guarding it now?"

"You'll have to ask Your Majesty that. If not for Your Majesty, how would this maid ever dare to speak this way?"

Her final syllables drifted upward slightly, and Chunluo tilted her head and batted her eyes, brimming with playfulness.

Prompted by this, Xiao Zheng's mouth curved slightly: "That is true. Since I favor you now, it wouldn't matter even if you were arrogant and domineering. But you must be careful—hmm, or perhaps you should try a little harder."

Chunluo was speechless; he could actually say something like that!

This showed that Xiao Zheng truly treated imperial concubines like monkeys playing tricks—oh no, he was simply toying with everyone around him.

This sort of person was simply too full from eating too much, coupled with having far too much power in his hands.

Moreover, the vibe of "Very well, you've successfully caught my attention" from old-school romance novels was an extremely fitting match.

While Chunluo muttered complaints inwardly, her outward expression remained radiant and sweet: "This maid will certainly try hard, so that Your Majesty cannot bear to punish me."

Xiao Zheng nodded lazily and raised his arms to stretch.

Chunluo rose right after him, standing by his side like a little follower.

Xiao Zheng tilted his head: "You really need to train your observational skills. Come here and untie my belt."

"—Your Majesty, in broad daylight, isn't this rather improper?"

Chunluo acted coy.

Xiao Zheng was left speechless: "...I need to change into informal attire."

"Oh... It was this maid who judged a gentleman's heart with her own petty measures. Please don't blame me, Your Majesty."

While speaking, Chunluo began unrobing him, her attitude of admitting fault lacking even a shred of sincerity.

Xiao Zheng felt a slight sense of puzzlement: Did he normally present himself as such a benign person? How did this little palace maid suddenly grow the guts of a bear and a leopard?

Having changed into casual wear, the time was approaching the *Si* period (9:00 AM), and Xiao Zheng began his morning meal.

Presently, having two meals a day was the norm, but powerful households naturally ate however many meals they wished.

Since Xiao Zheng had eaten some light snacks before attending the morning court, he wasn't particularly hungry right now. Chunluo, acting as his little shadow, was drooling with hunger, seeing as her stomach was completely empty.

"Pull back that look in your eyes. You look like you haven't eaten in three days."

Chunluo said in a soft, delicate voice: "If this maid hadn't eaten in three days, how could I still stand here watching with my own eyes?"

Su Youren and the other attendants waiting nearby thought: *Whoa, is she talking back to him? How—[

chapters.title: I want to indulge in broad daylight, what do you think?
chapters.content:
"Su Youren, bring her a set of tableware."

Xiao Zheng looked at Chunluo: "Sit down and eat."

Chunluo took her seat smoothly. This was against the rules, but since Xiao Zheng had already spoken, if she hemmed and hawed to decline, it would only annoy him.

Soon, the bowl and chopsticks were delivered. Chunluo picked up her bowl and dug in, occasionally using serving chopsticks to place a couple of bites onto Xiao Zheng's plate...

Uhm ⊙o⊙... She was thoroughly unceremonious and felt completely unfettered.

Xiao Zheng was somewhat at a loss to adapt. After all, someone who had always been so taciturn had suddenly become so... unrestrained? Lively? Bold? Relaxed? It was quite peculiar.

However, having seen too many pretentious, two-faced concubines and ministers, Xiao Zheng adapted after just a momentary flash of surprise.

After finishing the morning meal, Xiao Zheng paced back and forth with his hands behind his back along the corridors of the Hall of Mental Cultivation to aid digestion, and then entered the Imperial Study to start reviewing memorials.

As usual, Chunluo stood not far from the writing desk, lowering her gaze and keeping her eyelids drooped, maintaining the optimal posture of an ornamental vase at all times, because Xiao Zheng would lift his eyes to glance at her every now and then.

She was already quite proficient at this job. Maintaining her pose, Chunluo began browsing the system mall.

The mall was vast as an ocean, and those props were bizarre and varied, but browsing too much also became boring. It was a pity she couldn't read novels or binge-watch dramas; otherwise, her little daily life would still be quite fulfilling.

After taking a stroll around, Chunluo checked her two posted updates. The like count for the first had risen to 3,456, and the second had 4,567.

[Special Fever-Reducing Medicine] -100, [Plump Breasts and Rounded Hips] -50, [Bright Eyes and White Teeth] -50, [Mastery of Traditional Chinese Medicine] -2000, [Picture-Perfect Brows] -200, [Skin Smooth as Jade] -600, [Butterfly] -50. Her remaining points balance soared as high as 4,973.

After much deliberation, Chunluo still purchased one [Fertility Pill].

[Item Description

Name: Fertility Pill

Function: This is a consumable targeted medicine. After oral administration, it remains active in the human body for one natural month (30 days) and enhances sperm vitality.

Flaw: If the sperm itself is too weak, a 100% pregnancy rate cannot be guaranteed; if the sperm itself is too strong, multiple births are very likely to occur, causing excessive burden on the maternal body and making childbirth difficult. Please use with caution.

Price: 10 points.]

To be honest, turning even a fertility pill into a targeted medicine—Chunluo was thoroughly impressed.

As for the flaw... Although Xiao Zheng himself seemed quite robust, his little tadpoles probably weren't all that strong; otherwise, with so many concubines in the palace, why weren't several of them pregnant?

Chunluo had also watched popular science videos: the process of pregnancy was equivalent to a race of three hundred million little tadpoles cutting through thorns and thistles all the way, and whoever arrived first stood a chance of being born.

As long as Xiao Zheng's little tadpoles weren't exceptionally weak, she would definitely be able to conceive.

Although getting pregnant wasn't an ideal choice, once she was pregnant, surely she wouldn't still be chased off to Shuiyun Taoist Temple to become a nun.

For the sake of braised pork, she had no choice but to resort to this desperate measure!

Chunluo instructed the system to place the fertility pill directly into her esophagus so it would take effect immediately.

Speaking of the system's miraculous aspects, there was one delivery location worth praising: the items Chunluo purchased could be deposited at any time within a spherical range centered on her with a radius of five meters.

In other words, if Chunluo wanted to poison someone, she could completely manage to drop the poison out of thin air, and it wouldn't even be investigated.

This was simply a lethal weapon. As long as her heart was dark enough and her hand ruthless enough, this entire palace wouldn't be enough for her to kill!

Of course, Chunluo wasn't someone bloodthirsty and cruel. Up until now, she had only ever plotted against Xiao Zheng's third leg, and even then, she had been reprimanded and threatened by the system.

Chunluo could not help but sigh with emotion: No matter how many tricks one has, it's never as good as being born into a good womb.

Xiao Zheng, who had been born into a good womb, was currently frowning. Raising his eyes to look at Chunluo to clear his vision, he went back to reading the memorials.

Soon he frowned again. What was going on today? He had read several memorials in a row filled with nonsense. The Directorate of Ceremonies was truly a bunch of trash; why did they even send up this kind of memorial?

Or did the Directorate of Ceremonies think these memorials were also important?

Xiao Zheng slammed a memorial shut with a "clack," fire flaring in his heart. Was it his fault alone that he had no children? A whole bunch of concubines who only knew how to eat for free—hadn't he been trying?

The imperial physicians clearly said his body was very healthy! Otherwise, where had the eldest princess and the eldest prince come from?

At this thought, Xiao Zheng narrowed his eyes in deep thought: If the eldest prince hadn't been murdered, actually no ministers would have vaguely urged him in their memorials. It seemed he still had to find a way to manage those lawless concubines, lest all his hard work go to waste.

Yes, Xiao Zheng naturally knew that the eldest prince's accident certainly wasn't a simple one, and he had his suspects: Consort De and the Empress.

Although the eldest princess borne by Consort De had also been harmed, at the time the eldest princess and the eldest prince had fallen into the water together. Precisely because of this, Consort De's suspicion was even greater than the Empress's.

Because of this, Xiao Zheng had selectively favored a few more times the Empress's maternal cousin, Talent Liu, and Noble Lady Yao, who lived in the same palace as Consort De—he had done it purely on purpose.

When he mentioned earlier that he was picking someone, he was actually agonizing over it. After all, Talent Liu belonged to the Empress's faction, and if Noble Lady Yao were to get pregnant and give birth, by convention the child would be handed over to Consort De to raise.

As an emperor, Xiao Zheng was self-disciplined and diligent, and he also understood how to balance his court ministers; the inner palace was actually a microcosm of various factions.

Therefore, the Empress's clan could not be allowed to grow any stronger, so Talent Liu was ruled out.

And Consort De...

Xiao Zheng was not optimistic, only thinking of the worst: if Consort De were truly as ruthless as he imagined, capable of harming even her own biological daughter, then she deserved even less face, so Noble Lady Yao was ruled out as well.

The other concubines also had their respective factions, and the five newly entered noble ladies showed no signs of taking sides yet, but... Xiao Zheng didn't find any of them particularly pleasing to the eye.

Although he didn't find the other concubines pleasing either, those like Talent Liu and Noble Lady Yao who could provide him with other kinds of amusement made favoring them bear a tiny bit of interest.

After all, once that matter became tied to a task, even the greatest amusement would become utterly tasteless.

Dwelling on this, Xiao Zheng raised his eyes once more to glance at Chunluo—

This little palace maid was able to stir up his interest purely through her appearance, figure, and temperament. But since he had finally found someone pleasing to the eye, why toss her into the inner palace to be tainted by those bad habits...

Xiao Zheng stood up, walked over to Chunluo, cupped her face in his hands, and scrutinized her closely.

Chunluo obediently let him look. *Sigh, he's just looking at a vase, get used to it.*

"This face of yours..."

Chunluo waited for a moment, but the second half of the sentence never came. She quickly lifted her eyes to peek at him and asked in a delicate voice, "Your Majesty, what is wrong with this maid's face?"

"I want to indulge in broad daylight, what do you think?"

"............"

Chunluo was shocked, then speechless.

Then she held her breath, successfully blushing her face—pretending she had turned crimson with shyness—before standing on tiptoe, leaning forward, and pecking Xiao Zheng on the lips.

Xiao Zheng pulled her into his embrace and returned the kiss.

Kissing her, he walked toward the daybed in the inner chamber of the Imperial Study.

Chunluo obediently collapsed onto the daybed and reached out to untie Xiao Zheng's belt. Come to think of it, this belt was the one she had tied on him herself.

How could this not be considered beginning and ending with the same thing?

***

Extra Scene:

Belt: If I had sentience, I would definitely curse you two scoundrels! Doing lewd things in broad daylight, garbage is literally produced this way.

Lewdness: Can you use a different word next time you curse? They're the ones doing it, you didn't have to drag me into it. I was born to be done—[

chapters.title: What of an emperor possessing the entire world? He can't even eat a single lychee and toss away the
chapters.content:
In broad daylight, water was called for in the Imperial Study.

Su Youren made arrangements while clicking his tongue in wonder inwardly: This girl Chunluo is truly formidable; she actually managed to entice His Majesty into doing that deed right here in the Imperial Study. I must treat her with respect from now on.

Along with the hot water delivered into the Imperial Study came fresh clothing.

The two quickly tidied themselves up, turning back into impeccably dressed, respectable figures.

Xiao Zheng, lazy and fully satisfied, returned to sit before his writing desk and continued reviewing memorials.

Chunluo, still radiating the pinkish flush of spring, received preferential treatment and sat right beside Xiao Zheng to grind his ink for him.

Because she sat close and her eyesight was exceptionally good, Chunluo inadvertently caught sight of the contents on the memorial.

Uhm... It was written in Classical Chinese.

However, even though Classical Chinese was already a condensed language, it still spanned several full pages.

Chunluo, who had at least scored over 120 points in the Chinese section of the gaokao in her past life, carefully pondered it and roughly translated the text—

It was a whole bunch of empty drivel. The main points were praising His Majesty's diligence to the utmost, how prosperous and stable the Qianyuan Dynasty was under His Majesty's governance, and finally concluding with a question asking whether they should hold an imperial selection to choose some daughters of good families to enter the palace so His Majesty could continue the imperial bloodline...

It was a miracle Xiao Zheng could actually read through it.

Just as Chunluo was thinking this, Xiao Zheng slammed the memorial shut with a "clack" over there, his expression displeased.

Ah, well, indeed he found it annoying as well.

However, an emperor's professional ethics quickly kicked in. Xiao Zheng flipped that memorial back open, right to the very end—

She brushed a flying-dragon-dancing "Read" character, then tossed it aside.

Then she continued reading the memorials below.

Chunluo continued to peek—this was a memorial reporting that some areas in Jiangnan might suffer from floods this year, and it listed several precautionary preparations.

Not to mention, it was quite well-organized.

No wonder the Qianyuan Dynasty was prosperous and stable.

Xiao Zheng wrote a few sentences at the back of this memorial: Heaven and earth are ruthless and treat all things as straw dogs; floods are truly natural disasters. My beloved subject, you prepare for the rainy day and struggle against the heavens. This is truly my fortune and the blessing of the people of Jiangnan. When you return to the capital to report on your duties, I will surely have a long heart-to-heart talk with you over drinks.

Chunluo couldn't help glancing at Xiao Zheng: Good grief, with the people around him he has such a foul mouth, but with court ministers he speaks honeyed words. You really have a way.

Xiao Zheng naturally felt this gaze, stopped writing, and looked over. Realizing that Chunluo had seen the imperial memorial, he curved his lips into a smile: "What?"

Chunluo lowered her eyes and smiled faintly: "Your Majesty is matchlessly handsome, this maid was just looking."

Xiao Zheng sneered: "Heh, I saw your expression, still lying?"

"Then how would Your Majesty want this maid to answer? This maid is afraid that if she speaks the truth, she won't be able to serve Your Majesty anymore."

When Chunluo spoke such presumptuous words, she raised her eyes to stare at Xiao Zheng, putting on a wronged expression of "there's nothing I can do," matched with her naturally slightly sorrowful misty-smoke eyebrows, making her look pitiful and touching.

Xiao Zheng wasn't angry in the first place, and at this moment he felt the urge to exercise again.

But no, excessive indulgence harms the body, and the memorials hadn't been finished yet.

He reached out and pushed Chunluo's head away: "Stop putting on an act, go get a fresh cup of tea."

Chunluo had no choice but to get up, take the half-warm teacup from the table, and head out.

Right next to the Imperial Study was the small tearoom. Xiaachan was somewhat surprised to see her carrying the teacup over, because the tea had just been sent in not long ago, so it shouldn't be cold yet, nor should it have been finished.

Chunluo kept it brief: "His Majesty said to change the tea."

"Alright, I'll brew it right away."

Xiaachan got busy with nimble hands and feet. She had undergone special training, and the steps of tea-brewing flowed like clouds and running water, accomplished in one go.

随后, Chunluo carried the tea filled to seven-tenths and returned to the Imperial Study.

Xiao Zheng was lowering his head to read a memorial. Chunluo didn't make a sound, walked over leisurely, lightly placed the teacup back in its original spot, then sat down and continued to peek.

Her timing was unfortunate; Xiao Zheng had already finished reading this memorial, picked up his brush dipped in ink, and with flying-dragon-dancing strokes wrote a single character: Read.

Well, judging by this, it definitely wasn't any top-secret matter.

Just like that, Chunluo sat keeping him company for over three hours. During this time, the tea was changed several times, and she ate a few plates of pastries until Xiao Zheng finally finished reading all the memorials.

By this time, it was already the fourth watch of the Shen period (four o'clock in the afternoon).

If no unexpected government affairs popped up, Xiao Zheng the emperor was essentially off work.

One had to admit, Chunluo, who had to get up at 3 AM, sleep at 8 PM, and work the entire remaining time, felt a fierce wave of envy.

Oh wait, now Chunluo might have to attend to him in bed, so it wouldn't be sleeping at 8 PM anymore. Wuwuwu, working overtime without overtime pay—why isn't there a labor bureau and labor law here? She really wanted to sue him!

Chunluo angrily muttered to herself in her heart and furiously ate three lychees.

Xiao Zheng looked disgusted: "I know you've never eaten lychees, but can you be aware of your status?"

Which palace maid would eat three lychees in a row without peeling one for him?

Chunluo spat out the lychee pit and became well-behaved again: "This maid knows her wrong, this maid will peel a lychee for Your Majesty right now."

With that, she got up and stretched her demonic claws toward the tribute lychee tree that had traveled thousands of miles by boat to the capital. In two or three moves, she plucked a plateful (about a dozen), peeled them, and placed them in the porcelain plate before Xiao Zheng.

"Your Majesty, this maid just tasted one, it's exceptionally sweet. Have a taste."

"I eat them every year, do I need you to taste-test?"

"That might not be certain. The weather is unpredictable, who knows which year's lychees might be sour? It's better for this maid to test them first."

Chunluo continued peeling lychees, putting one in her own mouth and one in front of Xiao Zheng.

To be honest, ever since her transmigration, she hadn't really eaten much fruit. After all, it was an ancient world, and people ate whatever was in season. Besides, she was just a palace maid, and even dried fruit was something she could only look at.

Now it was great—she could even eat tribute lychees.

However, only twenty trees of the first batch of lychees had been shipped over, and currently there was no way to increase the yield. A single tree actually only bore a dozen to a few dozen lychees at most, and never more than fifty.

Take the lychee tree right in front of Chunluo, for instance; it generally only had about sixteen lychees on it.

And the ones that could be sent directly in front of Xiao Zheng were probably the ones with the most fruit among this batch of tributes.

It just goes to show, what use is it for an emperor to possess the entire world? He couldn't even afford to eat one lychee and throw one away, heh.

Although Chunluo's soul didn't have the audacity to eat one and throw one away back in modern times either, that was because she was frugal. At the very least, if she gritted her teeth, she could buy three or five catties and eat her fill...

Soon, the lychee tree was picked clean, leaving only a pile of peels and pits on the table.

Having eaten too much in one breath, Chunluo felt a bit cloying. She hurriedly poured herself a cup of plain water to drink, poured one for Xiao Zheng as well, and said with a caring expression, "Your Majesty, drink a sip of plain water to clear the rich taste."

Xiao Zheng: ...Most of the lychees went into your mouth, of course you feel cloyed.

However, he couldn't be bothered to mention this and instructed Su Youren beside him: "Pick out four trees with heavy fruit yields. Send two trees each to the Empress and the Imperial Noble Consort, and then harvest the rest according to the usual precedent and send them to various places."

Chunluo was somewhat curious about this—

After all, later generations always said that even the Empress could only eat a few lychees. She wondered how many were sent according to precedent.

chapters.title: Didn't we exercise in the morning? If we exercise again at night, I won't be able to take it.
chapters.content:
Waiting until Su Youren bowed and withdrew, Chunluo immediately asked out loud: "Your Majesty, what is the amount according to precedent?"

"Why ask about this? Still want to eat?"

Xiao Zheng sat casually, looking lazy and noble.

Chunluo reached out and hooked his finger: "This maid is just curious, Your Majesty~~~"

"...What kind of weird voice are you making?"

Xiao Zheng smoothly began to toy with her hand, which was as smooth as congealed fat and had a wonderful texture, and said casually: "The Empress in the palace gets 6, the Virtuous Consort gets 2, the Respectful Consort gets 2, Consort Xin gets 1, Lady Lin gets 1, and the rest get nothing. In addition, first-rank high officials get 2, and imperial clan marquises get 2 or 1 depending on their rank. After dividing them up, there should probably be a few dozen left over."

After hearing this, Chunluo had only one thought: It seemed she still had to bravely strive for the top and become the Empress Dowager after all, because that way she would at least have two lychee trees and a dozen or so lychees.

Of course, actually the best solution would be to develop technology and infrastructure.

Pity that Chunluo knew lychees could be artificially increased in yield, and she knew airplanes looked like they had big wings, but she didn't know how to specifically make them happen.

This couldn't be blamed on Chunluo either; after all, she had majored in computer science in university, and after graduation she passed the teacher recruitment exams and became a primary school teacher...

If she had known beforehand that she would transmigrate, she definitely would have memorized the manufacturing methods of the four great treasures: cement, glass, soap, and gunpowder. But she hadn't been given the exam questions in advance, so she transmigrated with an empty brain.

If there were zombies, even if they opened her skull they would probably shake their heads and leave in disappointment...

Chunluo couldn't help but sigh inwardly: One only regrets the books one has read too little when the time comes to use them.

"Why did you stop talking? What you just ate alone was more than all the six palaces of the East and West combined."

Chunluo sighed gloomily: "Never mind that lychee trees can't thrive in the north, that's a fixed rule, but why are there only a dozen or so on a single tree? Your Majesty, why don't you have the fruit farmers who grow lychee trees rack their brains to increase the yield?"

Xiao Zheng laughed in amusement: "You think they haven't tried to find ways? The ones that can be shipped to the capital are already top grade. If I speak up again, who knows what kind of chaos will break out down below."

At this, Chunluo didn't know what to say.

Xiao Zheng pinched her hand: "Following the example of superiors is already hard to curb. I certainly don't want to be cursed a hundred years later as a mediocre ruler who loved extravagance."

"Your Majesty is wise."

Chunluo offered a dry compliment.

Xiao Zheng let out a light cluck, not angry at all, and instead said again: "Actually, it's not that there aren't any with exceptionally heavy fruit yields, but those are all centuries-old ancient trees. It wouldn't do to dig them up just for the sake of gluttony, and they'd likely wither and die on the road..."

"So, Your Majesty, why don't you head down to Jiangnan and eat right by the trees!"

Chunluo couldn't help whispering temptation in his ear.

Xiao Zheng knocked her on the forehead: "You argued before when I said you looked like a sycophant. If I traveled out, do you know how much human and material resources it would cost?"

Chunluo shook her head on the outside, but in her heart, she had gained a new understanding of Xiao Zheng's professional ethics. Look, just look at how sober and self-disciplined this emperor was.

Xiao Zheng was still speaking lazily: "Actually, I don't really know either, but if the emperor travels in person, local officials and gentry will certainly rack their brains to come and kowtow, and who knows, they might even concoct some auspicious omens. Not only would it waste labor and money, but it would also breed corrupt officials... sigh."

Xiao Zheng actually wanted to go out and wander around too. The misty rain of Jiangnan, the boundless desert, the bright moon on the sea, and countless other sceneries written about by poets—he naturally wanted to see them with his own eyes.

Pity that in his eight years on the throne, Xiao Zheng only went out to ride horses and blow in the wind during the annual spring and winter hunts. The farthest place he went to was the imperial villa for summer retreat, which wasn't very far from the capital anyway.

However, Xiao Zheng merely felt a bit regretful about this and wouldn't act on impulse just because he felt tempted.

Chunluo didn't know what he was thinking, but she still listened with utmost admiration.

She said very sincerely, "Your Majesty, the phrase 'brilliant and martial' doesn't even do you justice anymore."

"Heh, need you to tell me?"

Xiao Zheng was obviously quite pleased with himself, patted Chunluo's hand, and ordered, "Give me a shoulder massage, and I'll let you keep eating lychees tomorrow."

"Thank you, Your Majesty!"

Chunluo began massaging his shoulders and, with a strong sense of customer service, asked if it was too light or too heavy, appearing exceptionally flattering.

At the fourth watch of the You period (six o'clock in the afternoon), Xiao Zheng had his evening meal.

A few dishes of the food sent by the imperial concubines were also selected and placed on the table. Chunluo couldn't sit at the table, so she stood to the side serving food.

Perhaps because she ate too many pastries at noon and the lychees in the afternoon were too sweet, she wasn't hungry at all right now, and the table full of rare delicacies didn't make her mouth water in the slightest.

When the meal was finished, the sky had already grown dark. Xiao Zheng waved his hand and dismissed Chunluo.

Barring any accidents, Chunluo got off work early today.

Since she wasn't very hungry, Chunluo went to the place where the palace maids were served food and ate a little casually, washed up, and then leisurely returned to her single room.

She wasn't very tired, but Chunluo still closed the door, took off her clothes, and lay on the bed closing her eyes to rest, while actually opening the system in her mind, preparing to draft and publish a post.

The likes on her previous two posts seemed to have saturated and wouldn't grow anymore without some stimulation.

After thinking it over and carefully deliberating, Chunluo published her third post:

【The Empress and the Great General had a secret rendezvous, resulting in two possible outcomes: either the ungrateful emperor gets cuckolded, or his own biological sister the Empress is sentenced to death.

To me, both were gratifying, so I pretended nothing happened and left directly.

But an accident happened. Not long after leaving the Baohua Hall, an imperial eunuch blocked my path and led me up to the opera tower.

The emperor, dressed in black casual clothes, was standing there with his hands behind his back, looking at... the Baohua Hall!

My heart shook violently, but with an expressionless face I offered my greetings. He turned around, smiled, and asked, "What did you see?"

Lowering my eyes and looking obedient, I suddenly understood: he had long known that his Empress was having a secret rendezvous with the Great General, yet he let it develop, and even chose the opera tower as the prime spot to watch...

I couldn't help feeling confused: Have I been dead for too long? Why can't I see through his thoughts at all?

Seeing me silent, he asked another question: "I'm asking you, what did you see?"

At this moment, I choose—

1. Tell the truth, and exaggerate with added details;

2. Reveal my identity, and ask for the reason;

3. Change the subject, and seduce the emperor;

4. Brush it off with perfunctory words, and continue to hide.

Friends, how should I choose?】

Although it wasn't explosive enough, keeping up the explosions would make it too fake. Chunluo felt it was better to write realistically so she wouldn't run out of things to make up later. Digging holes without filling them and getting chased down the internet by interstellar netizens wouldn't be good.

Having burned too many brain cells, sleepiness washed over Chunluo. She closed her eyes and intended to go to sleep, but just as she pulled the blanket over herself, a "knock-knock-knock" sound rang out.

Chunluo took a deep breath, flipped straight up, threw on her clothes, tidied herself up carefully, and then went to open the door.

She thought it was Su Youren again, but when she opened the door, she found it was Xiao Zheng.

"This maid offers greetings to Your Majesty."

Xiao Zheng uttered an "en", raised his hand to signal her to get up, and swept his gaze across the room.

Since Chunluo was about to sleep, naturally she hadn't lit the lamp. Right now, the room was illuminated solely by the light filtering through the open door.

But it was clear at a glance.

Then Xiao Zheng said: "The windows don't let enough light through, change them to cicada-wing gauze. The bed curtains are too thick, change them to soft smoke gauze. This room cannot be lived in today."

Chunluo: ...

A thousand words condensed into a single sentence—

Didn't we exercise in the morning? If we exercise again at night, I won't be able to take it.

chapters.title: Carrying the Vase Profession to New Heights
chapters.content:
Chunluo trailed closely behind Xiao Zheng step by step.

Soon, the two of them arrived at the sleeping quarters.

Xiao Zheng un-dressed of his own accord and urged Chunluo: "Take them off."

Chunluo now felt rather glad: her physical stamina was recognized by the system as good; sleep was sleep, who was afraid of whom?

So she shed her clothes in two or three moves, though out of shyness, she kept her sleeping robe on.

Xiao Zheng didn't boldly strip completely naked either; wearing his sleeping robe, he got into bed and lay down.

Chunluo was somewhat bewildered. Eh (⊙o⊙)... Could it be that she was supposed to take the initiative?

Thinking this, Chunluo climbed onto the bed, lay down right next to Xiao Zheng, turned on her side to press close, and hesitatingly stretched out her neck wanting to kiss Xiao Zheng.

"Behave yourself, unless you don't want to get out of bed tomorrow."

Chunluo, whose stamina was at 95, refused to submit: Who would be the one pinned down was yet to be decided!

However, Xiao Zheng's attitude was already very clear, so Chunluo had no choice but to obediently lie flat. Anyway, working overtime didn't come with overtime pay; no matter how good her stamina was, she was too lazy to take the initiative.

An evening without dreams.

At 3 AM, Chunluo woke up and found herself sleeping right at the edge of the bed, looking as if she was just one step away from rolling off.

Meanwhile, Xiao Zheng was sleeping right in the middle of the bed with extremely well-behaved sleeping postures.

Chunluo cautiously inched her way over, stopping only when her shoulder brushed against his, and then went back to sleep while giving herself a psychological suggestion: she must wake up at five o'clock.

Ahem, to be precise, she called out to the system and had it set an alarm.

At exactly five o'clock, Chunluo was woken up by a soul-shaking alarm. At the same time, Xiao Zheng, possessing a natural biological clock, gradually woke up. In the outer room, Su Youren's voice rang out:

"Your Majesty, it's time to rise."

Xiao Zheng opened his eyes, holding Chunluo in his arms.

Chunluo, who was being held, was very puzzled. She had woken up at 3 AM and hadn't slept deeply afterward; she felt like she had been lying flat the whole time!

Yet now she was being half-embraced by Xiao Zheng, and because they were pressed so close, the presence of his "weapon" was exceptionally obvious...

Xiao Zheng's voice was slightly hoarse: "Still not getting up?"

"This maid is getting up right now!"

Chunluo immediately got out of bed, washed up briskly, put on her clothes, and then began dressing Xiao Zheng, who had already finished washing up leisurely.

The full set of dragon robes worn for morning court was extremely cumbersome, but Chunluo had crammed the memories beforehand, so she wasn't flustered at this moment, and even appeared somewhat smooth and flowing.

Finally, she placed the crown with hanging pearls on Xiao Zheng's head, feeling a fresh sense of novelty and a sense of accomplishment akin to dressing up a life-sized doll.

Once Xiao Zheng was all tidied up, he headed to the Imperial Study to kick off a new day of work.

Only then did Chunluo tidy herself up, all while watching Su Youren direct the others to change the bed curtains in her room...

Once the interior was given a completely new look, it indeed looked much more elegant, and of course, much more expensive too.

After all, soft smoke gauze was light and had a draping quality; using it for bed curtains was using a sledgehammer to crack a nut. As for the cicada-wing gauze, it went without saying—it was a quite famous fabric. Using it to paper the windows did let light through, indeed, but it was just like something Xiao Zheng would suggest.

As the passive recipient, Chunluo couldn't say much either; she just felt that the gazes the palace servants of the Palace of Earthly Tranquility gave her grew even more respectful and flattering.

Chunluo wasn't the type to get carried away and run wild just because she gained favor. If they wanted to flatter, let them flatter; her attitude hadn't changed anyway.

Her main identity hadn't changed either, after all. If she wanted to act arrogant, she could only bully her colleagues, and wouldn't that just be bullying her own people?

Chunluo strolled around the Palace of Earthly Tranquility with nothing to do. Of course, she couldn't enter places she wasn't allowed to, so she just strolled along the courtyard corridors. One after another, several groups of people arrived at the doorway, all coming to offer tokens of goodwill.

Before long, the square table in the outer room was piled high with various kinds of food.

Chunluo touched her chin and thought, maybe she should express her goodwill too, otherwise it would look like she didn't care... but she didn't know how to do anything.

Although she had plenty of points now and could completely purchase some props, such as [Mastery of Classical Dance], [Culinary Mastery], or [Embroidery Mastery], Chunluo herself didn't actually like these kinds of "exercise".

Never mind, she'd rather read more books.

So Chunluo found a storybook to pass the time.
